units.text: Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java is a Java library that enables developers to create, read, and manipulate PDF documents without requiring external dependencies. It supports tasks such as adding text, images, form fields, and annotations to PDFs, as well as extracting content from existing files. Developers working in Java 11 or newer can integrate it using the org.aspose:aspose-pdf-foss package at version 26.8.0 under the MIT license. The library serves teams building applications that need reliable, self-contained PDF processing capabilities.

Create and modify PDF documents by adding pages with Page, inserting text fragments via TextFragment, and building table structures with Cell, Row, and Table objects, as demonstrated when populating a page with content or constructing form elements like radio button options.

Extract text and images from PDF pages using TextAbsorber for plain text retrieval and XImage iteration over page resources to save images to files, supporting both single-page and multi-page extraction workflows.

Work with AcroForm fields by accessing the document form through Form, reading and setting values for TextBoxField and other field types, and iterating over all form fields to inspect their names and current values.

Configure annotations and widget characteristics by creating WidgetAnnotation instances with specific rectangles, then customizing visual properties such as border color via getCharacteristics().setBorder() and background color via getCharacteristics().setBackground().
Reduce document size and protect content using built-in resource optimization and encryption features without requiring any external libraries.
Validate documents against PDF/A-1 through PDF/A-4 standards and convert them to those formats using dedicated validator and converter classes.
Create a page-level widget annotation and set its border color, then read it back:
The following workflows demonstrate common tasks with Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java, including adding interactive form elements, extracting text and images, and manipulating form fields.
Add a text label and radio button option to a table cell.
Extract all text from a PDF using TextAbsorber.
Save all images from a specific page as PNG files.
Create a new PDF with a single text fragment.
Populate form fields and iterate over all form fields.
Insert multiple radio button options into a cell in order.
Set and retrieve the background color of a widget annotation.
Configure and inspect the border style of a radio button option.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java provides the Document class as the central entry point for working with PDF documents, with page-level access through PageCollection and Page, and document-level operations exposed via facades such as PdfFileEditor, PdfContentEditor, PdfBookmarkEditor, PdfExtractor, PdfConverter, and PdfFileSignature. The library targets Java 11 and is distributed as the org.aspose:aspose-pdf-foss package at version 26.8.0.
The top-level namespace org groups the Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java module, with org.aspose providing the next-level package organization and org.aspose.pdf containing the core PDF processing types.
The getting started guide introduces the core concepts and initial steps for using Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java to process PDF documents.
The how-to guides and FAQ provide practical examples and answers to common questions about using Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java.
The full API reference documents every class, method, and behavior available in the org.aspose:aspose-pdf-foss package version 26.8.0.
The contributor guide explains how to set up a development environment and contribute code to the Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-Java repository.
The publishing guide describes the steps and requirements for releasing a new version of Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java.
The changelog lists all notable changes, bug fixes, and new features introduced in each release of Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java.
The getting started documentation walks through installing the library and performing basic PDF operations.
The text extraction documentation explains how to extract text content from PDF pages using the library.
The annotations documentation covers creating, modifying, and removing annotations such as highlights and notes in PDFs.
The attachments documentation shows how to add, extract, and manage file attachments embedded in PDF documents.
The forms documentation explains how to work with interactive AcroForm fields in PDF documents.
The XFA forms documentation describes support for reading and processing XFA-based forms in PDF documents.
The metadata documentation details how to read and update document properties and XMP metadata in PDFs.
The PDF/A documentation explains how to create and validate PDF/A compliant documents for long-term archiving.
The document conversion documentation covers converting PDFs to other formats such as DOCX, HTML, and images.
The document generation documentation explains how to build PDF documents from scratch using the library.
The drawing API documentation describes how to draw shapes, lines, and graphics onto PDF pages.
The facades API documentation explains how to use simplified high-level classes for common PDF tasks.
The navigation documentation covers creating bookmarks, destinations, and hyperlinks to improve document navigation.
The page operations documentation explains how to split, merge, rotate, and rearrange pages in PDF documents.
The rasterization documentation describes how to convert PDF pages to image formats such as PNG and JPEG.
The resource optimization documentation explains techniques for reducing file size and improving performance.
The digital signatures documentation covers applying and verifying digital signatures on PDF documents.
The security documentation explains how to set passwords and apply encryption to protect PDF content.
The limitations and out-of-scope features documentation lists features not supported by this open-source version.
The issue tracker allows users to report bugs, request features, and track progress for the Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-Java project.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java version 26.8.0 provides a Java library for creating, editing, and converting PDF documents, targeting Java 11 and above, and is distributed under the package name org.aspose:aspose-pdf-foss.
OCR, conversion to non-PDF formats beyond HTML/XML, conversion from non-PDF formats beyond HTML, full XFA form rendering, and 3D annotations or PRC/U3D streams are not supported.
A single Document instance is not thread-safe, requiring one Document per thread for parallel processing.

Text replacement with non-Latin scripts, resource optimization, tagged PDF structure coverage, and PDF/X validation and conversion are partially implemented, while PdfFileSecurity.setAllowExceptions throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Public-key-encrypted PDFs are supported through the ICustomSecurityHandler interface, but no out-of-the-box helper for common cases is provided.
PDF/X validation and conversion lack dedicated test coverage despite supporting the same Document.validate and Document.convert APIs used for PDF/A.
Basic stream recompression works for resource optimization, but advanced strategies such as image downsampling profiles and font merging across resources are limited.
Build and test Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java using Java 11 and the build tool defined in the repository's CI workflow at .github/workflows/.
This package provides open-source access to PDF processing capabilities; the commercial edition extends these features with additional processing options, advanced rendering, and enterprise support.
